newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah rises in late trading, swap down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah rises in late trading, swap down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah rose further against the dollar in active Wednesday trading on capital inflow from offshore investment houses, dealers said.
One major local bank dealer said the dollar was well supported at the 2,320.0 level at midday before that became the resistance level later on European selling.
He said Singapore operators were seen taking profit at that level but then unloaded dollars as European markets opened.
The dealer said it seemed to have been a repeat of the past two days when the rupiah appreciated early in the afternoon as London and other European markets opened.
Dealers said there was market talk of an inflow of fresh funds from European investment houses, mainly from London.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,318.0/19.0 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,321.0/22.00.
"Sentiment on the rupiah remains firm. Operators were also seen unloading swaps," the local bank dealer said.
Swap premiums fell as offshore operators sold forwards.
"They could not park all the money into rupiah-denominated papers, so they sold forwards for now," he said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,317.90/18.35 and 2,318.75/19.25, respectively.
The rupiah has risen steadily against the dollar since the central bank widened its intervention band last week to eight percent from five percent.
Some economists were worried over the possible implication for Indonesian exports of a strong rupiah against the dollar.
But a UBS report said it was not necessarily so as oil exports were not rupiah-based and traditional non-oil exports were suffering from non-currency woes such as labour costs.
"Indeed, a stronger currency would facilitate imports of capital goods and raw materials, necessary to support capacity expansion in emerging, higher value-added export areas."
"So far, however, there is no evidence of any shift from a stable real currency policy to a strong currency policy."
One economist said a stronger currency would also reduce imported inflation which was present due to rising investments.
Overnight swap was at 0.40/0.45 and tom/next at 0.35/0.45.
One-month swap fell to 14.30/15.00 from 15.25/16.25, two to 30.0/31.5 from 30.50/32.50, three to 45.5/46.5 from 47.00/48.005 and six to 94.5/95.5 from 96.00/97.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,311/2,503 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,311/2,359 on Wednesday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364.
